data.title: 'There is a need to deepen the F&O market': SEBI chairman Tuhin Pandey exclusive
data.description:
The Futures and Options (F&O) market has always been a topic of extensive discussion in the world of finance and business, and now more so than ever. The F&O space is high-risk, high-reward because leverage magnifies losses on small price moves; contracts expire with rapid time decay, among many other factors.

CANNOT SHUT DOWN A SEGMENT 

SEBI chairman, Tuhin Kanta Pandey, is of the opinion that there is a need to deepen the F&O market. According to the head of the market regulator, shutting down any segment by force is not the right approach.

He also spoke about how SEBI is actively working on the Pre-IPO market. According to Pandey, Long-Term Futures and Options should be available. Furthermore, touching upon the aspect of market regulation, he said that market regulation should ensure caution while also allowing the market to grow at the same time without many impediments.

The SEBI chairman was speaking at CNBC Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh Summit. In his address on the different intricacies of the market, he underscored the need for deepening the F&O market and advocated against 'shutting down' any segment.

REGULATION AND GROWTH 

He also spoke about how SEBI is actively working on the Pre-IPO market. According to Pandey, Long-Term Futures and Options should be available. Furthermore, touching upon the aspect of market regulation, he said that market regulation should ensure caution while also allowing the market to grow at the same time without many impediments.

After NSE's recent listing, he said that competition & cooperation between BSE and NSE are important.

In his address at the summit, Pandey also spoke about the APL Apollo-Tata Steel deal and said thatvsaid that it is pertinent to look into the deal and see whether the transaction comes within the Related Party Transactions (RPT) framework.

Furthermore, the SEBI head said that they will also look into aspects of corporate governance; they also added that if there are any pluses and minuses in corporate governance, the market regulator will take a look into the matter.

data.title: Solana News: Developers Issue Urgent Upgrade Notice to Mainnet Validators
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • Anza told Solana mainnet operators, staked and unstaked, to install Agave validator client v4.4.2 immediately.
  • The developers said the network was continuing to operate normally; the release does not by itself indicate an outage, exploit or attack.
  • The exact technical issue behind the urgent release has not been fully established.
  • Validator directory data shows mixed software versions, but no verified breakdown of v4.4.2 adoption is available yet.
  • The notice is aimed at node operators, not wallet holders, and does not by itself require SOL users to take any action.

Solana developers have issued an urgent instruction to network operators, asking them to install the latest version of the Agave validator client without delay.

The announcement from Anza, the development team responsible for maintaining Agave, applies to both staked and unstaked nodes running the affected software. The developers also indicated that the network was continuing to operate normally.

The announcement follows a series of Solana validator software improvements introduced earlier this month, including further development of Agave and Firedancer.

An urgent software update does not necessarily mean that a blockchain is experiencing an outage. In Solana’s case, the more interesting question is how quickly its distributed network of operators can respond when developers identify a problem that cannot wait for a routine upgrade.

What Is Behind Solana’s Urgent Upgrade?

Anza directed operators to install version 4.4.2 of its validator software, telling them in its announcement:

“

Don’t wait, upgrade now.

Anza · Agave v4.4.2 upgrade notice

The release is documented in Anza’s official GitHub repository, while compatible builds have also reportedly been made available by Jito-Solana and Harmonic.

Agave is one of the software implementations responsible for processing transactions and participating in Solana’s consensus mechanism. Validators running it help determine which transactions become part of the blockchain.

Unlike updating an application on a phone, updating validator software involves coordinating machines operated by independent organizations around the world. Developers can release a new version, but the operators themselves must deploy it.

Network monitoring data from Validator Info shows that both Agave 4.4.2 and Jito 4.4.2-jito have been released, while Firedancer’s latest listed version is 26.11.1. The availability of these releases does not, however, establish how many validators have installed them.

That makes the speed of adoption almost as interesting as the release itself.

A check of the Solana validator directory shows operators reporting different software versions, including Agave-derived implementations. However, a complete and independently verified breakdown of the latest upgrade’s adoption was not yet available.

The precise technical issue behind Anza’s urgent instruction remains to be fully established. Describing the release as a response to an exploit or an active network attack would therefore be premature.

Solana’s Recent Upgrades Face a Different Kind of Test

The announcement comes just weeks after Solana introduced significant changes to its underlying infrastructure.

As NewsBTC previously reported, the Solana Foundation introduced protocol version 1.0 in November and moved away from describing the network as mainnet beta.

The distinction between the protocol version and the validator software version is important. Solana can establish a common set of network rules while individual software implementations continue to receive updates and fixes.

The network has also been pursuing faster transaction processing and shorter confirmation times through its Alpenglow consensus architecture.

Those improvements are valuable, but faster transactions are only useful if the infrastructure processing them remains dependable.

What Does the Upgrade Mean for SOL Holders?

For ordinary users, Anza’s instruction is aimed at node operators rather than wallet holders. The announcement does not, by itself, establish a need for users to move their SOL or change how they interact with the network.

At the time of the dashboard snapshot, Solana had 655 active validators and five listed as delinquent. Approximately 423.44 million SOL was actively staked, representing 99.97% of the reported total stake. The figures offer a snapshot of network participation while operators are being asked to update their software, although they do not independently confirm the success of the upgrade.

The next meaningful development will be evidence that operators have installed the new release and that transaction processing remains stable throughout the rollout.

Solana has spent considerable time demonstrating how fast its network can become. This weekend’s upgrade offers another opportunity to assess something equally important: how well its infrastructure responds when speed is required outside of normal transaction processing.

data.title: India’s Water Adaptation Gap Spurs Push For Precision Farming, Restoration
data.description:
Aeroponics, sensor-based irrigation and community-led watershed management are emerging as approaches to address groundwater stress and climate risks to agriculture

India’s growing water stress and climate vulnerability are prompting calls for greater investment in precision irrigation, controlled-environment farming and community-led water restoration, as stakeholders seek to make agricultural practices more resilient to rising temperatures and erratic monsoons. With agriculture heavily dependent on freshwater resources, the challenge is increasingly shifting from awareness of climate change to implementing solutions that can conserve water, protect farm productivity and strengthen rural livelihoods. India recorded 10 of its 15 warmest years during 2011–2025, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

The winter season in 2025 also recorded its highest temperature anomaly since 1901, underscoring the growing climate pressure on agricultural systems. Arvind Narayanan, Co-Founder of Growize Farms, said the country's agricultural practices were developed for climatic conditions that are changing rapidly, making adaptation increasingly necessary. “India’s water and agricultural adaptation gap isn’t about awareness; it’s about action. Every farmer in the country is well aware that the seasons are getting hotter. Our farming system was designed for a climate that no longer exists,” Narayanan said. He said agriculture consumes over 80 per cent of India's freshwater resources, while nearly one in four groundwater blocks is already classified as semi-critical, critical or over-exploited.

Precision Farming And Water Efficiency

Narayanan said groundwater depletion required a shift in agricultural practices, particularly in crops that can be cultivated through controlled-environment systems. “Think of groundwater as a bank account where you've been taking out more than you've been putting in for decades. A good monsoon will top up the account, but it won't fix the model.

Wheat and paddy won't go into a controlled environment. Vegetables and leafy greens can and should,” he said. Growize Farms cultivates vegetables and leafy greens through aeroponic farming, a soil-less method in which plant roots are supplied with nutrient-rich mist. The company claims its farms use 95 per cent less water than soil farming, produce 36 times more yield per acre and enable year-round cultivation without pesticides.

“Growing more of this on precision farms with quick access to markets frees up water and land for staples. We have the technology. We just need the finance and policy to treat controlled-environment farming as climate infrastructure,” Narayanan said. Mallesh TM, Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of CultYvate, said irrigation efficiency was particularly important for water-intensive crops such as paddy and sugarcane, which he said consume close to 80 lakh litres of water per season per acre. “There is a need to grow both these with less water by irrigating when the crop actually needs it, not by habit or calendar,” Mallesh said.

CultYvate uses field sensors to track water-table levels in paddy and soil moisture in sugarcane, alongside satellite monitoring, to help farmers make irrigation decisions. In Punjab, the company said Alternate Wetting and Drying across more than 73,000 acres is saving around 930 cubic metres of water per acre, or about 15 per cent, while improving yields, reducing cultivation costs and lowering methane emissions and electricity consumption for groundwater pumping. In Tamil Nadu, the company said its sugarcane irrigation interventions have helped reduce water use by 60 per cent and increase yields by up to 50 per cent.

Community Action And Water Restoration

Water adaptation is also being pursued through ecological restoration and community participation, particularly in water-stressed regions. A Tata Communications spokesperson said the company integrates climate change, biodiversity, water and energy considerations into community initiatives, with partnerships focused on ecological restoration and regeneration. “Keeping the community at the centre of development is key.

Environmental CSR frameworks must be built to ensure that local Panchayats, women’s self-help groups, and youth become active custodians,” the spokesperson said. Through Project Nanneer, Tata Communications said it has enhanced the water-holding capacity and supported groundwater recharge of Nagan Thangal lake, improving livestock water availability, occasional fishing and community recreation.

The initiative has benefited nearly 12,000 individuals, 60 per cent of whom belong to marginalised communities, the company said. In Dharashiv, Maharashtra, the company's rural programme works with expert organisations on integrated watershed management, focusing on soil moisture retention, aquifer replenishment and climate-resilient farming. “These initiatives shield rural livelihoods from severe monsoon delays and chronic droughts,” the spokesperson said. The interventions highlight the need to combine farm-level technology with local water management and investment to improve agricultural resilience amid changing climate conditions.

data.title: Swara Baby Products Cuts IPO Size To Rs 800 Cr From Rs 1,000 Cr
data.description:
Under the OFS, Brainbees Solutions and promoter entity Anadya Bon Merchari LLP will sell shares worth Rs 150 Cr each

Swara Baby Products, the contract manufacturing arm of FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions, has reduced the size of its proposed initial public offering (IPO) to Rs 800 Cr from the earlier planned Rs 1,000 Cr, as per a media report.

According to the company’s red herring prospectus (RHP), the IPO will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 500 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 300 Cr.

Under the OFS, Brainbees Solutions and promoter entity Anadya Bon Merchari LLP will sell shares worth Rs 150 Cr each. Brainbees Solutions had initially planned to offload shares worth Rs 300 Cr through the IPO, while Merchari LLP had proposed selling shares worth Rs 200 Cr.

The company plans to use the fresh issue proceeds to establish a manufacturing facility in Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh, repay borrowings and finance potential acquisitions. It has allocated Rs 198.2 Cr for the proposed facility and Rs 127.5 Cr towards debt repayment, including borrowings of its subsidiaries.

The IPO will open for subscription on December 2 and close on December 4. The anchor investor bidding is scheduled for December 1. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 105-111 per share, valuing it at around Rs 3,211 Cr at the upper end of the band.

The shares are expected to list on the BSE and NSE on December 9.

Inside Swara Baby Products’ Business

Founded in 2018 by Alok Birla, Rahul Bubna and Ritum Jain, Swara Baby Products manufactures disposable hygiene products across baby care, incontinence and feminine hygiene categories. Its product portfolio includes baby diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins and panty liners.

The company primarily operates as a contract manufacturer for brands such as FirstCry, Piramal Pharma and Himalaya Wellness. It also markets products under its own brands, Cuddles for children and Shields for adults.

FirstCry acquired an initial stake in Swara Baby Products in 2020 and increased its holding over the years. According to the company’s draft IPO papers filed in July 2026, Brainbees Solutions held a 76.6% stake in Swara Baby Products.

Swara Baby Products reported consolidated operating revenue of Rs 1,163.9 Cr in FY26, registering a 23.4 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase from Rs 943 Cr in FY25.

Its net profit rose 18.5 per cent YoY to Rs 95.6 Cr in FY26, compared with Rs 80.7 Cr in the previous fiscal.

For Q1 FY27, the company reported a net profit of Rs 16.6 Cr and operating revenue of Rs 322.9 Cr.

data.title: Commercial Vehicles To Post Double-Digit Growth In November: Nuvama
data.description:
Freight activity supports commercial vehicle demand, while passenger vehicles and two-wheelers are expected to register more moderate volume growth in November

India's commercial vehicle market is emerging as the strongest pocket of growth in the automobile sector, with domestic volumes projected to expand at a double-digit pace in November. Passenger vehicles and two-wheelers, meanwhile, are likely to register more measured gains, according to an assessment by Nuvama Institutional Equities, cited in a media report.

Commercial vehicle (CV) volumes are estimated to increase 11 per cent year-on-year (YoY) during the month. The projection reflects a relatively firm freight environment, with trends in electronic way bills and freight rates pointing to sustained movement of goods across the road network.

Tata Motors is expected to remain among the key beneficiaries of this demand cycle. Its domestic CV volumes are estimated to rise 18 per cent YoY to around 41,800 units. Eicher Motors' commercial vehicle business, VE Commercial Vehicles, could record 15 per cent growth at about 8,800 units, while Ashok Leyland is projected to post an 11 per cent increase to nearly 20,300 units.

The divergence between commercial and consumer-facing vehicle segments offers a broader read on the underlying demand environment. CV demand tends to track freight utilisation, industrial activity and the movement of goods, making the segment an important indicator of economic momentum.

Passenger Vehicle Growth Moderates

Passenger vehicle (PV) volumes are expected to expand 8 per cent YoY in November, although the performance is likely to remain uneven across manufacturers.

Mahindra & Mahindra is projected to lead the segment with 25 per cent growth at 116,800 units in domestic volumes, followed by Tata Motors at 17 per cent at 69,000 units. Hyundai Motor India is expected to record 9 per cent growth at 73,000 units, while Maruti Suzuki could see volumes rise by around 2 per cent at 233,000 units.

The PV market continues to receive support from product launches, improving vehicle affordability and relatively accessible financing. However, the estimates indicate that market growth is becoming increasingly differentiated across manufacturers rather than moving uniformly across the segment.

Two-Wheeler Demand Stays Firm

Two-wheeler volumes are expected to register 7 per cent YoY growth in November. Royal Enfield is projected to record 19 per cent growth, while TVS Motor could post a 15 per cent increase. Bajaj Auto's volumes are estimated to rise 8 per cent, with Hero MotoCorp expected to grow 4 per cent.

Export markets are likely to remain an important component of the growth equation for several manufacturers. Domestic demand, meanwhile, continues to provide a stable base as rural and urban consumption conditions improve at different rates.

Tractor Market Faces Headwinds

The tractor segment presents a contrasting picture. Nuvama expects volumes to remain broadly unchanged in November as regional weakness and an elevated base weigh on demand.

Western and southern markets are facing softer conditions, while last year's state-level subsidies have created a comparatively demanding base for year-on-year comparisons. Rainfall deficiencies and pressure on farmers' terms of trade from higher fuel costs could further constrain demand.

data.title: Dunzo Co-Founder Kabeer Biswas’ AI Startup M Raises $9 Mn In RTP Global-Led Round
data.description:
The latest funding comes around seven months after M raised USD 11 Mn in a seed round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Blume Ventures and fintech company CRED

Dunzo co-founder Kabeer Biswas’ AI startup M has raised USD 9 Mn (Rs 82 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by venture capital firm RTP Global, as per a media report.

Existing investors, including Peak XV Partners and Blume Ventures, also participated in the round, doubling down on their earlier investments.

With the latest fundraise, M’s total capital raised has reached around USD 20 Mn.

The latest funding comes around seven months after M raised USD 11 Mn (around Rs 102 Cr) in a seed round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Blume Ventures and fintech company CRED.

Founded in December 2025 by Biswas and former Swish executive Kartik Mishra, M currently offers access through a waitlist. While details about its services remain limited, the startup had earlier said it planned to integrate AI into the kitchen to help households manage routine decisions, coordination and everyday services.

“We will make modern living feel frictionless and fundamentally transformed,” the startup’s description reads.

In June, M was reportedly serving around 150 households in Bengaluru as part of its early rollout. The startup was also exploring a subscription-led business model, targeting affluent urban households.

Biswas co-founded hyperlocal delivery startup Dunzo in 2014. After a brief stint at Flipkart Minutes, he launched M to explore AI-powered household management.

Dunzo, which had raised capital from Reliance Retail, shut down its operations in 2025 after facing mounting cash burn, operational challenges and intensifying competition in the quick commerce market.

Biswas joined Flipkart in 2025 to lead its quick commerce business, Minutes, but exited the company in October that year.

With M, Biswas is attempting to build a new consumer technology category around AI-powered household management, moving beyond the delivery-led convenience model that defined his earlier venture.

data.title: Vodafone Idea Names Former Mahindra CFO Parthasarathy V S To Board
data.description:
The appointment brings experience in financial management, mergers and acquisitions, and corporate governance

Vodafone Idea has appointed Parthasarathy V S as an Independent Director to its board in November 2026, bringing experience across financial leadership, telecommunications, information technology and corporate strategy. The appointment adds to the board’s expertise as the telecom operator navigates infrastructure requirements, technological changes and evolving customer needs.

Parthasarathy previously held several senior leadership positions at the Mahindra Group, including Group Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Group Chief Information Officer (CIO) and President of the Mobility Services Sector. He was also a member of the Group Executive Board, overseeing responsibilities across finance, technology, mergers and acquisitions, and business operations.

Leadership At Mahindra Group

During his tenure at the Mahindra Group, Parthasarathy held roles spanning financial management, information technology and business leadership. His responsibilities across multiple functions provided experience in strategic decision-making, operational management and corporate transformation.

His background in finance and technology is relevant to the telecommunications sector, where operators must manage network investments, digital infrastructure and changing business requirements.

Experience Across Company Boards

Parthasarathy currently serves as an independent director on the boards of PGP Glass, NIIT, Cloudnine Group of Hospitals and the Self Employed Women’s Association (SEWA).

His previous board positions include Allcargo Logistics and Mahindra Logistics, where he served as Chairman. These appointments have added board-level experience across logistics, education, healthcare and other business sectors.

Roles In Industry Bodies

Earlier in his career, Parthasarathy served as President of the Bombay Chamber of Commerce and Industry and worked as an Associate Director at Xerox.

His experience across industry representation and corporate leadership has included business management and corporate affairs, alongside his responsibilities in finance and technology.

Focus On Telecom Challenges

Vodafone Idea operates in a sector requiring sustained investment in network infrastructure, service capabilities and digital offerings. Its business spans mobile voice and data services, with network operations covering 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G technologies.

Parthasarathy’s appointment brings experience in financial oversight, strategic planning and governance to the board as the company addresses the operational and investment demands of a changing telecommunications market.

data.title: IAM Conference Highlights Aeromedical Support From Runway To Orbit
data.description:
Experts explore the evolving role of aerospace medicine in military aviation, civil aviation and human spaceflight.

The Institute of Aerospace Medicine (IAM), Bengaluru, hosted the 65th Annual Conference of the Indian Society of Aerospace Medicine (ISAM) on 26–27 November 2026, focusing on the expanding role of aeromedical support across aviation and space missions.

Themed 'One Airspace - One Mission: Aeromedical Support from Runway to Orbit', the conference highlighted the need for an integrated approach to aerospace medicine, covering military aviation, civil aviation and human spaceflight. It emphasised the importance of medical support in ensuring aircrew safety, operational efficiency and human performance in increasingly complex aviation and space environments.

Inaugurated by Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Chief of the Air Staff, the conference brought together Defence Forces personnel, Indian Air Force aircrew and experts from the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL).

The scientific discussions examined emerging challenges in aerospace medicine, including altered gravity, spaceflight medicine, crew performance optimisation and the psychological demands of civil aviation. Experts also discussed indigenous aircraft design, safety considerations associated with ejection and extreme environmental conditions, and the integration of terrestrial simulations with orbital flight requirements.

The conference further explored the evolving role of women in fighter aviation and featured research presentations by young investigators, highlighting emerging developments in the field.

Addressing the gathering, Air Marshal Vivek Hande, Director General Medical Services (Air), emphasised the role of aerospace medicine in maximising aircrew efficiency and supporting the viability of human life in orbit.

The conference underscored the growing convergence of aviation and space medicine, highlighting the importance of scientific research, technological advancement and coordinated aeromedical support in preparing for future missions.

data.title: Indian Navy Receives Final Project 17A Frigate Vindhyagiri
data.description:
With 75 percent indigenous content, the frigate marks a milestone in India's warship-building capabilities and self-reliance.

The Indian Navy received Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024), the seventh and final ship of the Nilgiri-class Project 17A stealth frigates, from Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) in Kolkata on Friday. The delivery marks the completion of all seven Project 17A frigates and represents a significant milestone in India's indigenous warship design and construction capabilities.

Vindhyagiri is the third Project 17A frigate built by GRSE. Designed by the Warship Design Bureau (WDB), the ship incorporates advanced stealth features, weapons, sensors and automation systems, enhancing its operational capabilities across multiple maritime warfare domains.

The Project 17A frigates are multi-mission platforms designed to address current and emerging maritime security challenges. Compared with the earlier P17 (Shivalik)-class frigates, these ships feature an advanced suite of weapons and sensors, strengthening their anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine warfare capabilities.

The frigate is equipped with a Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) propulsion system, comprising a diesel engine and a gas turbine that drive a Controllable Pitch Propeller (CPP) on each shaft. It also incorporates an Integrated Platform Management System (IPMS) to support its advanced operational and automation requirements.

Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the ship carries forward the legacy of the INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate that served the Indian Navy from 8 July 1981 to 11 June 2012, completing 31 years of service to the nation.

With the delivery of Vindhyagiri, all seven Project 17A frigates have been delivered to the Indian Navy within 23 months of the first ship, INS Nilgiri, which was delivered on 20 December 2024. The construction period of Vindhyagiri was also reduced to 68 months, compared with 84 months taken for the first-in-class INS Nilgiri, reflecting the experience and efficiencies gained during the construction of the preceding six ships.

The project has achieved 75 percent indigenous content and involved more than 200 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). It has also generated employment for approximately 4,000 personnel directly and over 10,000 personnel indirectly. The delivery highlights India's growing capabilities in indigenous naval design, engineering and shipbuilding, reinforcing the Indian Navy's commitment to Aatmanirbharta in defence manufacturing.

data.title: L&T Bags 300 MW Battery Storage Order For Gujarat Project
data.description:
The Khavda project will provide three-hour storage capacity, helping manage surplus renewable electricity and improve grid flexibility as India expands clean energy infrastructure

Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has secured a significant order to develop a 300 megawatt (MW)/900 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery energy storage system (BESS) at Khavda in Gujarat, strengthening its position in India's growing energy storage market. The project, jointly secured by L&T's Renewables business and L&T Electronic Products & Systems, is designed to store surplus renewable electricity and release it during peak demand.

The order, announced on 25 November 2026, falls under L&T's significant order category, valued between Rs 1,000 crore and Rs 2,500 crore under the company's internal classification. The exact contract value has not been disclosed. The three-hour storage facility will have a power capacity of 300 MW and energy storage capacity of 900 MWh, enabling it to support the grid during periods when renewable generation fluctuates or demand rises.

Liquid-Cooling Technology To Support Grid Flexibility

The proposed battery system will use liquid-cooling technology, which L&T said would support higher power density, improved safety and a longer operating life. The technology is intended to manage heat generated during battery charging and discharging, helping maintain operational performance. Battery energy storage systems (BESS) are increasingly being deployed to address the mismatch between renewable energy generation and electricity demand.

Solar and wind output fluctuate with weather conditions and time of day, creating a need for infrastructure that can store electricity when supply is abundant and release it when demand increases. According to the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), India is projected to require 47.24 GW of battery energy storage capacity by 2031–32, with estimated investments of about Rs 3.49 lakh crore. The requirement is part of the country's wider push to integrate more renewable power into the electricity grid and improve reliability.

Storage Investments Gain Momentum

The Khavda project comes amid increasing investments in battery storage infrastructure as India advances its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity by 2030. Industry experts note that the expansion of renewable energy will increasingly depend on complementary infrastructure, including battery storage, transmission networks and grid management systems. Storage projects can help reduce renewable power curtailment, improve electricity supply during peak periods and support the commercial viability of clean energy assets.

L&T said the order strengthens its presence in the energy storage sector and reflects its capabilities in executing complex infrastructure projects at scale. The project is expected to improve grid flexibility and enable greater integration of renewable energy into India's power network.

data.title: SEBI chief exclusive on APL Apollo-Tata Steel, says will look into corporate governance, RPT framework
data.description:
SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey, in his latest remark on the ongoing controversy surrounding the APL Apollo-Tata Steel Deal, has said that it is important to see whether the transaction comes within the Related Party Transactions (RPT) framework.

Pandey also added that if there are any pluses and minuses in corporate governance, the market regulator will take a look into the matter.

The chairman of SEBI was talking at CNBC Awaaz's Market Mahakumbh Summit.

SEBI SUMMONS APL APOLLO

Meanwhile, on Friday, November 27, following concerns raised by minority shareholders, as per a Moneycontrol report, SEBI summoned senior officials of APL Apollo Tubes to explain the structure of its proposed transactions with Tata Steel.

As per the report, SEBI may also summon Tata Steel officials to explain the deal.

The market regulator is examining whether the arrangement breaches related-party transaction (RPT) rules, sources familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol.

On Friday itself, APL Apollo Tubes Ltd said the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) had extended the deadline for Tata Steel Ltd’s open offer to acquire up to a 26% stake in the company. The tubes and pipes maker said that the deadline has been moved from December 1 to December 8.

In a regulatory filing, APL Apollo said Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, the open offer’s manager, received the market regulator's approval by email on November 27 after Tata Steel submitted a request.

The offer covers the acquisition of up to 7.28 crore fully paid-up equity shares in APL Apollo, representing 26% of its expanded voting share capital. Each share has a face value of ₹2.

data.title: Binance gets preliminary approval to establish Asia hub in Bhutan
data.description:
Binance said on Friday it received in-principle approval from Bhutan's Gelephu Central Bank to establish regulated digital-asset operations in the Himalayan kingdom, as part of its plans to expand into five Asian markets next year.

"The in-principle approval is a first step, not a full license and Binance must satisfy the conditions specified by GCB ... before the relevant regulated activities may commence," the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said in a statement.

Binance's expansion push follows a security breach US authorities have linked to North Korea that resulted in $6.3 billion being stolen from its platform last month and stopped all users from making withdrawals for the next two days. The company said earlier this week it has finished work to recover its withdrawal systems.

This month, SB Seker, head of Binance's Asia-Pacific unit, told Reuters: "We have ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets ... three of which are in quite mature stages."

Seker did not specify the new markets that Binance was looking at. Binance has operating licences in 15 markets, and Seker said South and Southeast Asia were key priorities.

The partnership in Bhutan will include an operational presence, with local hiring and investment in digital assets, the Binance statement on Friday said.

"Establishing an Asia hub in Gelephu Mindfulness City is a strategic decision that reflects Binance’s commitment to operating within clear, progressive regulatory frameworks", Seker said in the statement.

Binance has said it could cover the losses linked to the October cyberattack without raising fresh funds.

data.title: Dan Ives Sees ‘Rollercoaster Ride’ Ahead For AI Stocks, But Says Nvidia Bull Case Remains Intact — ‘Our Stress Test Stands’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives acknowledged that a "rollercoaster ride" lies ahead for AI stocks, particularly with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang preparing to face lawmakers in Washington next week.
  • However, he said his investment thesis remains unchanged, including his conviction in Nvidia and other companies benefiting from the AI infrastructure buildout.
  • Ives believes China's contribution through the Asia loophole represents a manageable risk rather than a threat to the broader AI investment cycle.

The artificial intelligence trade could face more turbulence as investors weigh uncertainty around data center spending, China-related restrictions and the cost of financing the massive infrastructure buildout.

However, Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives isn't backing away from his bullish outlook, arguing that even a combination of adverse scenarios would not derail the AI revolution over the next several years.

Nvidia shares gained nearly 1% in Friday’s regular session, but edged lower by 0.5% during the after-hours trade.

Ives Puts AI Boom Through 3-Part Stress Test

In multiple posts on X on Friday, Ives acknowledged that a "rollercoaster ride" lies ahead for AI stocks, particularly with Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang preparing to face lawmakers in Washington next week.

However, he said his investment thesis remains unchanged, including his conviction in Nvidia and other companies benefiting from the AI infrastructure buildout.

Ives outlined three potential setbacks to test the resilience of the AI investment cycle, namely, 20% of planned data centers never getting built, revenue through the Asia export loophole disappearing entirely, and financing for AI infrastructure being curtailed by 25%.

Even under those conditions, Ives said he remains bullish on the AI investment thesis over the next two to three years.

Why Ives Isn't Worried

Ives believes China's contribution through the Asia loophole represents a manageable risk rather than a threat to the broader AI investment cycle.

He estimated that China and the Asia loophole account for no more than 15% to 20% of revenue, suggesting that even losing that business would not fundamentally change his long-term outlook.

Data center construction is another major concern for investors, particularly amid growing political opposition and questions about whether technology companies can sustain their enormous capital expenditure plans.

However, Ives' stress test assumes that one-fifth of these projects never materialize, alongside a 25% reduction in financing. His argument is that the AI opportunity remains compelling even if the infrastructure expansion encounters significant setbacks.

He also pointed to next week's congressional proceedings involving Huang as a major moment for the technology sector, saying the Nvidia CEO carries the weight of the broader AI investment thesis into Washington.

Ives Previously Called AI Sell-Off One Of The Most 'Disconnected' He's Seen

Ives' latest comments build on his recent defense of the AI trade amid a broader technology stock sell-off.

During an interview last week, he described the downturn as one of the most "disconnected" technology sell-offs of his career, arguing that investors were pricing in a scenario where the AI revolution simply disappears.

"These stocks are almost pricing in that the AI revolution doesn't happen, that it basically goes away," he said.

Ives also argued that the industry remains in its early stages, estimating that the AI revolution is less than 15% complete.

He pointed to persistent chip demand, saying buyers looking to order AI processors could face wait times extending until the end of 2028. He also noted that roughly 75% of data center projects were already permitted.

"This is not the end. This is just a turbulent, scary time for investors where it's all kind of come to a head here," Ives said.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.41%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) declined 0.06%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) gained 0.23%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) gained nearly 4% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) rose over 2%.

data.title: CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index sinks to 10 as extreme fear drags on
data.description:
CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index printed a score of 10 on November 28, 2026. That puts it in the "Extreme Fear" zone, near the bottom of a scale that runs from 0 to 100.

The duration matters as much as the score. The gauge has stayed below the extreme fear threshold of 25 for approximately 16 consecutive days, so crypto traders have now been nervous for over two weeks without a break.

A post on X described this as the crypto market's longest stretch of extreme fear. It also noted that half of the market's extreme-fear days have landed in just the last 10 days.

CoinMarketCap isn't the only tracker showing this. Alternative.me, which runs a separate sentiment index, reported readings clustered between 10 and 12 over the same period.

Prices explain much of that. Bitcoin traded in a range of roughly $59,756 to $61,549 in late November 2026. One reported analysis put Bitcoin's decline over the prior 30 days at 25.98%.

The year as a whole looks bad too. Alternative.me's data shows 154 days classified as extreme fear in 2026, and the calendar year hadn't yet reached December.

A sentiment index is a thermometer for the market's nerves. It doesn't measure price directly. It combines several signals that tend to move when traders get anxious or excited.

CoinMarketCap's version draws on several inputs. One is the price momentum of the top-10 crypto assets, with stablecoins excluded. Others are the implied volatility of Bitcoin and Ethereum, options put/call ratios, and Bitcoin's market cap measured against major stablecoins. User engagement on trading platforms also counts.

Implied volatility reflects how big a price swing options traders expect in the future. When it jumps, the market is bracing for turbulence.

The put/call ratio compares bets on falling prices with bets on rising ones. A high ratio means more traders are buying downside protection.

Comparing Bitcoin's market cap with stablecoins shows where money is sitting. When capital moves into dollar-pegged tokens, it is often waiting on the sidelines instead of taking risk.

More broadly, daily and intraday trackers like CoinMarketCap and Alternative.me pull together signals such as volatility, momentum, social activity and Bitcoin's market dominance. A reading of 10 means almost all of them point the same unhappy direction.

Crypto has seen extreme fear before. The 2022 collapses of Terra and FTX are the clearest recent examples. In both cases, sentiment crashed as prices fell sharply and confidence disappeared.

A few signals are worth watching from here. One is whether the CoinMarketCap and Alternative.me indexes climb back above 25, which would end the current extreme fear streak. Another is whether implied volatility on Bitcoin and Ethereum starts to cool, which would suggest traders expect calmer conditions.

Stablecoin balances are another clue. If capital that fled to dollar-pegged tokens starts moving back into Bitcoin and other major assets, the index's market cap comparison would begin to shift.

For now, the gauges agree. The crypto market is in one of its longest stretches of deep fear, and 2026 has already given traders 154 such days on Alternative.me's count.

data.title: Trump Crypto News: World Liberty Financial Sells $20 Million in Ethereum Assets, Data Shows
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • A wallet linked to World Liberty Financial sold 10,600 WETH and 1,378 mETH for about $20.06 million.
  • Proceeds went into about $17.58 million USDC and $2.48 million USD1, the project’s own stablecoin.
  • On-chain analyst Ember estimates a cost of $3,244 per ETH against a disposal value near $1,655, implying a loss of about $19.26 million.
  • The loss is an on-chain estimate, not an audited figure, and the sale covers one wallet rather than the project’s full holdings.
  • The move reverses earlier Ethereum buying, and there is no verified evidence that Donald Trump personally directed the trades.

Trump-backed crypto project World Liberty Financial has reportedly reduced its Ethereum exposure by approximately $20 million, converting two large holdings into dollar-pegged stablecoins during the latest cryptocurrency market downturn.

Blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain reported that a wallet associated with the project sold 10,600 ETH and 1,378 mETH, receiving approximately $20.06 million.

Separate estimates from on-chain analyst Ember suggest the assets may have been sold at a loss of more than $19 million.

The transactions come just weeks after World Liberty Financial announced a WLFI token buyback program, which could be partly funded by income generated from its USD1 stablecoin reserves.

The Ethereum sales represent a notable reversal for a project that previously accumulated the cryptocurrency during periods of market weakness. Where the money went, however, deserves just as much attention as what was sold.

World Liberty Financial Moves Into Stablecoins

The reported transactions involved approximately $17.58 million in USDC and another $2.48 million in USD1, World Liberty Financial’s own dollar-pegged stablecoin.

Transaction records from Arkham show a series of transfers between World Liberty Financial’s labeled Strategic Reserve wallet and CoW Protocol, involving outgoing mETH and incoming USD1. The wallet also interacted with decentralized lending protocol Dolomite.

The Ethereum assets included wrapped ether, known as WETH, and mETH, a token representing exposure to staked Ethereum.

The latter distinction matters because a liquid staking token does not necessarily trade at a one-to-one ratio with ETH. Simply adding the number of WETH and mETH tokens together can give a misleading picture of the underlying Ethereum exposure.

According to Ember’s estimates, the combined holdings represented approximately 12,121 ETH in equivalent exposure.

The analyst estimated an average acquisition cost of $3,244 per ETH, compared with an average disposal value of approximately $1,655.

If that cost-basis estimate is accurate, the transactions would represent a loss of roughly $19.26 million, or close to half the original investment.

TransactionReported figure
Sold10,600 WETH + 1,378 mETH
Ethereum-equivalent exposure≈12,121 ETH
Received$17.58M USDC + $2.48M USD1 = $20.06M
Estimated average cost$3,244 per ETH (≈$39.3M)
Average disposal value≈$1,655 per ETH
Estimated loss≈$19.26M (about 49%)

World Liberty Financial’s reported Ethereum sale. Cost basis and loss are on-chain estimates, not audited results. Data: Lookonchain, Ember. Visualization: NewsBTC.

World Liberty Financial has not been shown to have confirmed that loss in a public accounting statement. The figure remains an on-chain estimate rather than an audited financial result.

Why the USD1 Transaction Matters

World Liberty Financial’s decision to move part of the reported proceeds into USD1 raises questions beyond the performance of its Ethereum investments.

In its official USD1 risk disclosures, World Liberty Financial acknowledges that its financial interests and those of BitGo may differ from those of USD1 holders. Both benefit from net fees earned through interest on the stablecoin’s reserves, while USD1 holders are not entitled to those earnings.

That makes USD1 more than another cryptocurrency held in the project’s treasury. It is part of the business through which World Liberty Financial seeks to generate revenue from its digital-dollar product.

Holding USD1, however, does not automatically generate a return for the wallet that receives it. Nor does an exchange of existing tokens necessarily increase the stablecoin’s circulating supply or reserve income.

The relevant question is whether the transactions represent temporary treasury management or a broader change in the project’s investment strategy.

A Reversal of Its Earlier Ethereum Strategy

In January, NewsBTC reported that World Liberty Financial had acquired approximately 2,868 ETH after selling more than $8 million worth of wrapped Bitcoin.

The November transactions point in the opposite direction, with the reported wallet moving away from Ethereum-linked exposure and toward dollar-denominated assets.

It would nevertheless be misleading to conclude that World Liberty Financial has abandoned Ethereum entirely. The activity concerns a specific wallet, and the project’s broader holdings across other addresses have not been established by these transactions.

Data from Arkham Intelligence shows that the project’s labeled Strategic Reserve wallet held approximately $243.8 million in digital assets on November 28. Notably, more than 96% of that valuation came from its own WLFI token, while the wallet retained 2,000 ETH worth approximately $3.32 million.

The concentration raises a separate question about the reserve’s exposure to fluctuations in the price of its own token. Its reported portfolio value should not necessarily be confused with readily available liquidity.

There is also no verified evidence that President Donald Trump personally instructed the trades.

For Ethereum investors, the reported sale is another example of a large crypto-linked entity reducing exposure during a difficult market. For World Liberty Financial’s stakeholders, the more consequential questions concern its treasury strategy, the management of investment losses and the transparency of its financial disclosures.

The blockchain can reveal how assets moved. It cannot, on its own, explain who authorized those movements or why.

data.title: Michaël van de Poppe Says Bitcoin Could Hit $100,000 In First Quarter Of 2027
data.description:
Key points:
  • Analyst Michaël van de Poppe says there can be a two-stage Bitcoin bounce.
  • He said the process will start with a rapid relief rally, then a steeper rise after the Nasdaq bottoms out. 
  • Bitcoin is trading under its 200-day moving average, which is a measure of the digital currency's average price over the past 200 days.

Bitcoin (BTC) could jump back to $100,000 in the first quarter of 2027, analyst Michaël van de Poppe said, attributing its drop toward a two-year low to Nasdaq selling rather than any crypto-specific problems.

The selloff has been an “extreme outlier,” Van de Poppe, founder of MN Capital, said during a Thursday appearance on Bitcoin Magazine’s BMTV. He foresaw a two-stage Bitcoin bounce, starting with a rapid relief rally, then a steeper rise after the Nasdaq bottoms out.

Selling Related To Stocks

The Bitcoin drop is not very much related to the crypto industry, said Van de Poppe. He said it is being sold by institutional investors to hedge risk in other holdings, and in a panic, everything falls together. Gold, silver, AI stocks, and Bitcoin are all down in the latest rout.

Van de Poppe said that Bitcoin behaves like stocks when the markets change. “It still trades like a risk-on asset," he said. He added that Bitcoin trails when stocks bounce back, since asset managers require more confidence before buying it back. He thinks it will take a few days of the Nasdaq being up before money flows back into Bitcoin ETFs.

"The recent drop was the kind of move you get about once a year," he said. Such moves tend to trigger a 15% to 40% short-term rally, which would put Bitcoin at $68,000 to $72,000, he said.

ETFs Cut Both Ways

Van de Poppe also said that the bull markets of 2024 and 2025 only happened because money poured into ETFs. “If not for this, Bitcoin would probably stay in a bear market for four to five years, trading around $20,000 to $30,000,” he said.

That flow has now reversed. Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost about $5.7 billion in November through Friday, beating the previous record of $4.51 billion set in June, SoSoValue data showed.

Four To Eight Weeks

The analyst said, "A lasting recovery will take longer.” Bitcoin is trading under its 200-day moving average, which is a measure of the digital currency's average price over the past 200 days. It needs to get back to that level and to its 21-week average, which has typically taken four to eight weeks, he said. The setup, he said, was reminiscent of late 2015, when a similar shakeout led to a sharp rally.

He also expects the next bull market to match 2017 rather than deliver smaller gains. Stablecoins, tokenization, and AI agents finally give crypto real use outside its own industry, he said, comparing the moment to the early days of Apple’s (AAPL) iPhone.

Van de Poppe dismissed concerns that AI or quantum computing could break Bitcoin. The network has already survived a lot, he said. “If the agentic era or quantum can break Bitcoin, I think we have way bigger problems to deal with,” he said.

Calls For A Rebound

He has been calling for a rebound for weeks. Earlier this month, he said Bitcoin could recover after Anthropic's (ANT) IPO, as it did after SpaceX's (SPCX) listing in June.

Bitcoin’s price was down over 3% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC moved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘normal’ from ‘high’ over the past day.

data.title: The Graph to Activate REO Step 5 on December 8th
data.description:
The Graph will activate REO Step 5 on December 8th. Indexers with more than 30 million GRT in total stake will need to serve qualifying queries on one subgraph per 3 million GRT, up from one per 4 million GRT; all other indexers will retain the 10-subgraph minimum.

Refer to the official tweet by GRT:

The Graph
@graphprotocol

REO Step 5 starts December 8

Indexers above 30M GRT total stake will need to serve qualifying queries on 1 Subgraph per 3M GRT, up from 1 per 4M GRT. Every other Indexer keeps the 10-Subgraph minimum.

Nov 27, 2026

GRT Info

The Graph is a decentralized protocol designed for efficient data indexing and querying from public blockchains. One of the functional elements of The Graph is subgraphs. Subgraphs are created by third-party developers to receive and index data from specific blockchains.

The Graph (GRT) is a utility token used within The Graph ecosystem. The Graph Foundation issues grants in GRT to subgraph developers and other tools. GRT holders can also delegate their tokens to curators or indexers to participate in network security and receive a share of rewards for curation or indexing.
